title: The Koehler cryptograms, Abwehr Hamburg -> Paris, February 1944 (Kahn, Cryptologia 5(2), 1981)
system.summary: Letter cipher with near-flat letter counts (IC 0.0398); monoalphabetic, transposition, periodic, autokey, standard-tableau running key, Gronsfeld and Enigma excluded; mixed-tableau running key or one-time pad remain.
system.sibling_key: Hoover (1946) names a book cipher on a Dutch prayer book for the FBI-run Koehler channel; the book is not identified. Not used.
system.notes: Chi-squared 57.9 against uniform (c low, z high) excludes machine output; no depth between messages.
conditions.prior_solution.where: No reading known; Schmeh Top 50 no. 47 lists it as unsolved
conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.
conditions.tools: IC and periodic statistics (periodic.py); quadgram hill-climb, German/English/Dutch (lm.py); running-key likelihood test against simulated controls
outcome.method_basis: Ciphertext-only statistics and solvers on Kahn's 1981 Cryptologia text excluded monoalphabetic, transposition, periodic polyalphabetic, autokey, standard-tableau running key, Gronsfeld and Enigma; no plaintext or key was found.
outcome.contribution: none
outcome.notes: Skipped as intractable: mixed-tableau running key or one-time pad, no crib. Reopens with the FBI case file, Kahn's source file or the prayer book.
solution.kinds: transcription; statistics; solver; hypothesis; statistics; literature search
doc.shelfmark: British archives copy published by Kahn, Cryptologia 5(2), April 1981 (reference unknown); messages 237, 178, 137, 140, 229
doc.plaintext.source: No plaintext published; the FBI plaintexts of the Koehler channel are not public.
doc.transcription.source: Kahn, Cryptologia 5(2), 1981, checked against the printing (msgs.py)
doc.transcription.notes: Five messages of 237, 178, 140, 140 and 229 letters; the one headed 137 has 140. Count 924 / 26 distinct measured with --measure --letters on a scratch export of msgs.py (the text lives in a Python file). One correction: message 137 group 17 is ayddq, not ayddg.

title: The 22 'unsolved' ADFGVX radio messages, Eastern Front, November 1918 (Childs corpus; Schmeh's list)
system.summary: ADFGVX: 6x6 Polybius substitution to letter pairs followed by columnar transposition under a three-day key (lengths 16-19).
system.sibling_key: Fourteen published period keys (Lasry, Niebel, Kopal, Wacker) plus Lasry's sixteenth CHI key of 13 Nov 1918 from the 2017 thread, rebuilt here; used.
system.notes: Three published squares damaged by PDF dash collapse and repaired; transposition convention settled on page 100.
conditions.prior_solution.where: Published keys (Lasry et al.) and the 2017 comment thread under Schmeh's post (9 solved, 3 partial)
conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.
conditions.tools: ADFGVX decoder (adfgvx.py, repair.py); block-edit search with German quadgram model (blocks.py, lm_de.py); gap-aware annealer (gaps.py); key-free transposition annealer (keyless.py) with planted controls
outcome.method_basis: The fourteen period keys published by Lasry, Niebel, Kopal and Wacker for the Childs corpus, plus Lasry's sixteenth (CHI) key from the 2017 Cipherbrain comment thread, were applied with a block-edit search; the only full reading (page 100) had already been read in 2017.
outcome.contribution: key extended or corrected; catalogue correction
outcome.notes: Nothing read here that the 2017 readers had not read; the thread consolidated and the sixteenth key rebuilt. Ten messages remain open, needing the Childs originals or an unlisted key.
solution.kinds: key from source; verification; literature search; solver; solver; control
doc.shelfmark: James Rives Childs transcription, pages 73-217 (list provided by George Lasry on Schmeh's blog, 2017)
doc.plaintext.source: Readings of 9 messages and parts of 3 in the comment thread under Schmeh's 2017 post (Norbert, Armin, Lasry and others); 10 never read.
doc.transcription.source: Schmeh's blog page (msgs.txt), from the Childs transcription
doc.transcription.notes: Count is the sum of the per-message letter counts in the NOTES table (22 messages, marked gaps excluded). msgs.txt mixes blog prose with the ciphertext, so --measure gives no clean figure. Mutilation in transmission (lost or added letters, marked gaps) is the obstacle.

title: Adrian of Utrecht, the Admiral and the Constable of Castile to Charles V, Vitoria, 30 Dec 1521, AGS Estado leg. 8 no. 150
system.summary: Mixed nomenclator: two- and three-letter code groups for words and syllables with initials in plaintext-alphabet blocks, plus a homophonic alphabet of letters, figures and signs.
system.sibling_key: Adrian's own dotted trigraph code (PTR 2/1/94-101) and the Estado 8/112 sign cipher checked: different systems, not used.
system.notes: Triple-barred staff and P4 open and close paragraphs. Code-group initials follow the alphabet in blocks (r a-, f c-, l d-f, ... x v-y); order within a block not recoverable.
conditions.prior_solution.where: Danvila, Memorial Historico Espanol 38 (1899), pp. 703-705 (Gredilla's decipherment)
conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.
conditions.tools: PARES image fetcher (pares.py); chunk alignment on xif = V. M. anchors (chunks.py)
outcome.method: key recovered based on plaintext from external sources
outcome.method_basis: The ciphertext was aligned chunk by chunk with Gredilla's 19th-century decipherment printed by Danvila (Memorial Historico Espanol 38, 1899, pp. 703-705), found during the attempt; the code and part of the alphabet were rebuilt from that alignment and used to read or correct about 17 of the roughly 25 groups the print left blank.
outcome.contribution: transcription; key recovered
outcome.notes: Read in full via the 19th-century decipherment, checked and corrected; about ten groups open (suf, xub, yo, ren nod, xac, sif, tib, xit, Lag, ne).
solution.kinds: access; literature search; transcription; sibling key; reading; prediction; verification
doc.shelfmark: AGS Estado leg. 8 no. 150 (PARES 13002542)
doc.plaintext.source: Claudio Perez Gredilla's decipherment, printed by Danvila, Memorial Historico Espanol 38 (1899), pp. 703-705, with about 25 groups unread
doc.transcription.source: PARES images (~1000 px), crop and upscale
doc.transcription.notes: --measure gives 1312 whitespace tokens / 575 distinct, but sign runs are written as single {braced} tokens and clear words are mixed in, so the enciphered-token count is not known. Several sign readings still rough; alphabet homophones not separated.
system.diacritics.note: A sign suffix on a code group marks inflection (mix la / mix= las).

title: Cardinal Barberini to Nuncio Ceva, Paris, 1632-34 (ASV SdS Francia 346)
system.summary: Homophonic substitution on two-digit figures with syllable and common-word codes, two-digit nulls (every pair beginning 2), '6' as word separator, and three-digit nomenclator elements formed of a prefix digit plus an ordinary two-digit code.
conditions.prior_solution.where: George Lasry reconstructed the key of this dossier on 24 Oct 2020 and it is attached to every DECODE record R74-R84 (DOC_R*_D32*.txt). He also published aligned decipherments of four of the eleven letters - 346:1 (R74), 346/4 (R77), 346/5 (R78), 346/9 (R82) - which covers three of the five ciphertexts this target names. He did not decipher R75 or R84, and left all 95 nomenclator elements he met unsolved. R75 additionally carries a contemporary interlinear decipherment made in 1632.
conditions.inputs: transcription; published key; published reading; cleartext context
conditions.human_role: Set the target; supplied nothing further. DECODE was reached with a cookie already in the repository.
conditions.tools: beam-search decoder over the digit stream (decode.py); character n-gram LM, lang/it-cinquecento interpolated with an in-domain model (indomain.py); leave-one-document-out calibration (eval.py); alignment against the 1632 interlinear (control.py, resolve.py)
outcome.method_basis: Lasry's reconstructed key (24 Oct 2020) is attached to every DECODE record R74-R84 of this dossier; it was applied with an LM beam decoder to R75 and R84, which had no published reading. The 1632 interlinear on R75 was used only as a control and to fix six nomenclator codes.
outcome.contribution: decipherment with ambiguous key; key extended or corrected
outcome.verification: contemporary decipherment; key confirms; historical consistency
outcome.notes: R75 and R84 read here for the first time; R77, R78 and R82, the other three ciphertexts this target names, were already read by Lasry in 2020. 0.92 is the share of enciphered tokens given a value; the independent measure of accuracy is the 77.5% letter agreement with the 1632 interlinear on R75. About three nomenclator elements in ten are still missed by the decoder, and a missed element is rendered as plausible Italian letters rather than as a gap, so errors concentrate there. 117 of the 123 nomenclator elements met in the dossier remain unread, and the people and places of both letters are inside them. R75 (25 Sept 1632) argues that the Swedish victories make an accommodation easier but the union far harder, and presses the French court to see how dangerous that power's reach towards the Mediterranean is to France itself. R84 (18 Dec 1632), a month after Lutzen, turns on 'quella vittoria' and ends with the Roman fear that the consequences will hold France disunited and unable to help her allies. The transcriptions are DECODE's and were not re-checked against the images. Measured 21 Sept 2026: 0.914 of tokens get a value. fraction_coherent 0.775 = the letter agreement with the 1632 interlinear on R75 (the only independent check). codes_open counts R75/R84 only (68 of 73 distinct elements met); dossier-wide 117 of 123.

title: Robert Fagel (The Hague) to Prince William V, 18 June 1804 (KHA A31 PWV inv. 337; DECODE R2238)
system.summary: Numerical code of 2-4 digit groups up to 2510, commas between words and dots joining groups within a word, clear endings (t, e, s) appended to some groups, embedded in a clear French letter.
system.sibling_key: none
system.notes: Keys tested and ruled out: the Stadholder's Grand Chiffre of 1782 (DECODE R1024, Euler); its instructions require a start letter when the additive Tableau is used, and R2238 has none, while direct lookup is nonsense. Also ruled out: R2233 (1801 small homophonic system), the 1790s Orange name key R2240, Dutch codebooks R1035 (1803) and R1891 (1798), and siblings R2236/R2237/R2239 in the same old inventory number.
conditions.prior_solution.where: DECODE status non-decrypted; no decipherment on the letter

conditions.tools: DECODE API and filesrv image download; PIL deskew and line crops; key lookup and Tableau start-point brute force (python)
outcome.method_basis: The 128 code groups on DECODE R2238 were transcribed, and every candidate Orange, Fagel and DECODE key of 1780-1815 (the Grand Chiffre R1024 with its tableau and renumberings, R2240, R1035, R1891, R2842-R2852) was ruled out; no key or clear copy was located.
outcome.contribution: transcription; catalogue correction

title: Alchymey teuczsch, alchemical recipe book, East Bavaria 1426, Heidelberg Cod. Pal. germ. 597 (DECODE R2876)
system.summary: Three simple sign alphabets for German (key A, the compiler's 24-sign 'new abc' of f. 1r; key B, stroke and figure signs of ff. 6v and 91v; set C of ff. 1r, 5v-6r, 44v, 93r), used for substance names inline in clear recipes and for a few whole passages.
system.sibling_key: none; the three sets share a b c d e and differ for i, n
system.notes: distinct_symbols is key A (24 signs incl. sch and ch). Key B has 19 values fixed from Wattenbach's f. 6v plaintext, with medial and final s as different signs; set C is fixed for 11 letters. Key A m-ch graded lower (read from shape under the strike).
conditions.prior_solution.where: Wattenbach 1869 (broke and described the ciphers, facsimiles and plaintexts of ff. 1r, 5v, 6v); Eis 1957/1982; Heidelberg catalogue 2014 (reads f. 93r). DECODE R2876 'Non-decrypted' is stale.
conditions.inputs: images; published reading; key from archive
conditions.human_role: Project-level: set up Claude Code with Opus 5 and posed the oldest-cipher candidate list (oldest/CANDIDATES.md A4). Images are free (no login). No target-specific intervention recorded in NOTES or git.
conditions.tools: lines.py (ink-profile line detection); seg.py, seg2.py (connected-component glyph boxes, strike-line removal)
outcome.method_basis: Wattenbach broke the ciphers in 1869 and printed plaintexts of ff. 1r, 5v, 6v, and the 2014 Heidelberg catalogue reads f. 93r; the project recovered the sign alphabets from the images by aligning them with those printed readings (external plaintext) and the compiler's own f. 1r alphabet.
outcome.contribution: key extended or corrected; catalogue correction
outcome.notes: Read by Wattenbach 1869; added here: the alphabets recovered from the images and checked, set C partly fixed, the survey, the folio correction. Open: no continuous transcription of the recipe cipher (ff. 7r-22r, 46r-v, 54r-61r), f. 9r ll. 7-12, the f. 6r glossary or f. 44v; key A m-ch unchecked on running text. NOTES has no '## Remaining gaps' section.
solution.kinds: access; literature search; statistics; key from source; verification; crib; crib
doc.shelfmark: Heidelberg UB, Cod. Pal. germ. 597 (DECODE R2876)
doc.route: not applicable (a recipe book, not a letter)
doc.plaintext.source: Wattenbach, Anzeiger fuer Kunde der deutschen Vorzeit NF 16 (1869), cols. 264-268 (plaintexts of ff. 1r, 5v, 6v); Eis 1957/1982 extracts; Kalning, Miller, Zimmermann, Cod. Pal. germ. 496-670 (2014), pp. 257-260, quotations resolved, incl. f. 93r
doc.transcription.source: Heidelberg digi.ub IIIF images (Public Domain Mark), 85 written leaves; glyph boxes by seg.py/seg2.py, enlarged strips
doc.transcription.notes: No continuous transcription of the cipher was made; only the alphabets (f. 1r, f. 6v, f. 91v) and check words (f. 1r l. 2, f. 11r, f. 93r) were transcribed sign by sign, so no token count exists. The survey of all 85 leaves locates the cipher runs.
system.diacritics.note: Set C distinguishes a box with one dot (e) from a box with two dots (t); dotted-box variants in the f. 6r glossary are not assigned.

title: Johann Heinrich Kauderbach (The Hague) to Dresden, 1754-56, intercepted despatches with passages in figures (KHA Prins Willem V inv. 201, DECODE R1043-R2082)
system.summary: Two-figure letter-and-syllable cipher, one code per value (about 60 codes), written without separation, with the digits 5 and 8 as nulls and names in clear capitals.
system.sibling_key: Kauderbach's 1761 key, HStAD 10024 Loc. 08236/11 Bl. 5 (DECODE R936): same design and vocabulary, different numbers.
system.notes: Names are capitals with ./. in clear (S./., Q./., P./.), meanings differing from the 1761 table. 13 may be y and re.
conditions.prior_solution.where: DECODE notes that the Hague cabinet never solved them; no printed decipherment found.
conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login and passed its session cookie to the model, set up Claude Code with Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal. No target-specific intervention recorded.
conditions.tools: curl (DECODE); python
outcome.method_basis: Nulls and the two-figure code table were found by statistics, and the code values were recovered by simulated annealing onto the plaintext vocabulary (letters and syllables) of Kauderbach's 1761 key (DECODE R936), whose numbers do not fit this 1754-58 table.
outcome.contribution: transcription; key recovered
outcome.notes: fraction_read = share of the 8,512 groups carrying a key value (only 10, 20, 40, 90 guessed, 12 occurrences). Readers estimate 65-97% of the text read in sense per letter; R1954 weakest; the clear sigla are read from context only.

outcome.contribution: transcription; key recovered; catalogue correction
outcome.notes: Unpublished cipher, opened 2026-09-20. TWO records carry the clerk's own full contemporary clear version - R9644 (ff. 241-242, in lettered sections keyed to the cipher) and R9650 (f. 272) - and R9648 is R9644's duplicate. R9652 carries no cipher at all - DECODE's 'partially decrypted' is wrong, the leaf is entirely in the clear - and is read complete too. Those four letters are therefore READ COMPLETE as to content (read_r9644.md, read_r9650.md): the Pope Adrian VI temporising between Charles V and Francis I, the French resolved to come into Italy with a great sum of money to Lyon, Hieronymo Adorno's intercepted letters, the Pope's parsimony and his unpaid household, the peace track through the archbishop of Bari. The CIPHER is read in part: 47 CODE values fixed against that plaintext and 29 probable (the 10 substitution-alphabet signs were downgraded to probable on 20 Sept after an 8x zoom showed signs that must be different letters looking near-identical at the zoom they were read at; the code groups, being plain latin trigrams that cross-check, are unaffected), kept apart in a confidence column and audited for conflicts. The key reads outside its own evidence - two thirds of tokens on sight in R9648 and R9650, and 'el papa' unaided in R9656, which has no clear version and no duplicate. Open: the five records with no clear version (R9634, R9645, R9646, R9649, R9656), and a word-perfect edition of any ciphered leaf, which needs the substitution alphabet - all ten alphabet signs probable after the 8x zoom on perdido, the rest limited by per-glyph discrimination on these scans.

system.sibling_key: None needed: the same key serves Spagna 364C (items 1-32) and 364D (items 1-24), 1717-1720.
system.notes: Nomenclator runs: 4001-4078 particles and endings; 4079-4296 nouns and names A-R; 4401-4479 S-V; 4485-4531 calendar and day numbers; 4532-4543 and 4552-4563 two parallel Gennaio-Dicembre month runs; 4535-4619 a second alphabetical run A-T; scattered blocks at 4681, 4706, 4870+. Lasry's filed key gives 268 of the 399 four-digit groups used in the corpus; 61 more were recovered in this session, leaving 135 distinct groups (3.4% of nomenclator tokens) without a value. The digit 3 is a null, except when it falls among the three digits following a 4 prefix, where it belongs to the nomenclator group.

outcome.contribution: key extended or corrected; catalogue correction

outcome.notes: Solved by George Lasry in October 2020 and already read on the DECODE records when this session began; nothing about the system was open. Verification detail: coverage measured token by token off Lasry's aligned decipherment; each recovered group rests on two or more independent contexts and usually the alphabetical bracket; 4538=Luglio matches the known date of Alberoni's promotion, 12 July 1717.

system.summary: Tomokiyo's Nevers-Piles symbol alphabet with homophones and code signs for common words and titles, used for short runs in a clear French letter.
system.sibling_key: Tomokiyo's partial Nevers-Piles table (from fr. 3612 f. 9, not digitised) and BnF fr. 4715 f. 2 (Guise to Nevers 1586, same cipher, interlinear decipherment; ~50 words aligned in fr4715_f2_aligned.txt); both used. The three keys bound in fr. 3413 (nos. 53, 61, 69) do not fit.
system.notes: Some values disagree between Tomokiyo's table and the cribs (his b=u, m=r, 8=c; cribs give p, o, t); in fr. 4715 plain m is r, in no. 62 tailed m is o. Signs are letter-shaped glyphs, digits and graphic signs; symbol_kind approximates this mix. 22 Sept: 41 distinct signs in no. 62 (measured). Homophones confirmed: n = ◻/Ħ/H, o = tt/m(tailed)/⋕, m = ∇/x, e = θ/æ, i = 9/ħ/ɸ, u/v = ɔ/φ/b. Codes: ⌘ = Mr, Ƒ = le, n = et, ʃ = jay, 1 = de.

title: Pallotto to Barberini, 1629 - 28 ciphered despatches of the nuncio at Vienna (BAV, Barb.lat. 6960)
system.summary: Two-digit homophonic substitution with syllable and common-word groups, three-digit nomenclator groups (200-999) for names and titles, and the digits 1 and 8 as nulls/word separators, written as a contiguous digit stream; the same key as Barb.lat. 6956 (1628), broken by Norbert Biermann and Thomas Bosbach in 2018.
system.sibling_key: Barb.lat. 6956 (1628), key recovered by Norbert Biermann and Thomas Bosbach, March 2018, filed on DECODE R215 (DOC_R215_D1506/D1507/D1508). George Lasry identified years ago that 6960 uses the same key; DECODE was never updated. Applied here 21 Sept 2026: it reads 6960.
system.notes: 112,805 digits over the 28 ciphertexts. Digit frequencies are uneven (0 = 16.1%, 4 = 4.8%) and adjacent digits carry ~0.18 bits of mutual information, so the stream is structured. No phase preference was found for two-digit codes (IC 0.01462 at phase 0 vs 0.01466 at phase 1; even- and odd-position digit distributions agree to 0.2%) or for three-digit codes - though that phase test is inconclusive on its own, since ~1.7% digit slips randomise the phase; the calibrated corpus search is the sound version of the claim. distinct_symbols is the digit alphabet, not the key's code groups, which are unknown. A run-length control puts the longest consistent two-digit alignment to the known plaintext at 39 letters against a chance baseline of 36-39, where a synthetic two-digit cipher at the same transcription noise gives 207 - so the stream is not a two-digit substitution of that plaintext. CORRECTION 21 Sept 2026: the variable-length diagnosis was right, the rest of the system was not identified here. The key (sibling, 6956) mixes two-digit homophones, three-digit nomenclator groups and one-digit nulls 1/8, which is why every fixed-width test failed and why the repeat spectrum showed deterministic variable-length groups. distinct_symbols stays the digit alphabet; the key has ~127 known entries.

outcome.notes: Contents in print since 1897 (Kiewning). The key was not recovered by this project: every attack here failed. It is the key of the sibling volume Barb.lat. 6956, broken by Biermann and Bosbach in 2018 and on DECODE R215; George Lasry had identified that it also serves 6960. Applied 21 Sept 2026, it reads all 28 ciphertexts except ~1,750 three-digit nomenclator groups absent from the key. The earlier finding of deterministic variable-length groups stands and is explained by the key (2-digit + 3-digit + 1-digit nulls). The catalogue said 'what the cipher hides is not known'; it is known, and has been in print since 1897, from the Roman office's own decipherments. The cipher itself was not broken here and no partial key is claimed: a held-out test shows the table learned from R286 predicts unseen text no better than a shuffled control (0.355 vs 0.359), so the 55% consistency of the first pass was overfitting. A positive control on synthetic ciphertext recovers a random key 100/100 from a clean transcription, 87/100 at 0.5% digit error and 7/100 at 1.7%, so the method is sound and the limit is the transcription. Two explanations remain open and cannot be separated from this material: length errors in the transcription, or the cipher not being a fixed-width substitution of this plaintext. The run-length control then settled that: the longest consistent two-digit run is 39 letters against a chance baseline of 36-39 (synthetic at the same noise: 207), so there is no alignment signal and noise is not a sufficient explanation. R286 is not a two-digit homophonic encipherment of Kiewning's Nr. 153. Open: whether the code width differs, whether the sheet encodes another despatch or a materially different wording, or whether the system is nomenclator-heavy or variable-length. A corpus search over all 1,161,303 letters of the edition then closed the first two: at widths 2, 3 and 4 no window of R286, R292, R306 or R311 enciphers any text printed in the volume, against a calibrated expectation of ~8 zero-false-positive hits on R286 alone. What survives is either a variable-length nomenclator, or text that is not in print because Kiewning gives it only as German regest.

title: Pallotto to Barberini, 1629 - 28 ciphered despatches of the nuncio at Vienna (BAV, Barb.lat. 6960)
system.summary: Two-digit homophonic substitution with syllable and common-word groups, three-digit nomenclator groups (200-999) for names and titles, and the digits 1 and 8 as nulls/word separators, written as a contiguous digit stream; the same key as Barb.lat. 6956 (1628), broken by Norbert Biermann and Thomas Bosbach in 2018.
system.sibling_key: Barb.lat. 6956 (1628), key recovered by Norbert Biermann and Thomas Bosbach, March 2018, filed on DECODE R215 (DOC_R215_D1506/D1507/D1508). George Lasry identified years ago that 6960 uses the same key; DECODE was never updated. Applied here 21 Sept 2026: it reads 6960.
system.notes: 112,805 digits over the 28 ciphertexts. Digit frequencies are uneven (0 = 16.1%, 4 = 4.8%) and adjacent digits carry ~0.18 bits of mutual information, so the stream is structured. A run-length control puts the longest consistent two-digit alignment to the known plaintext at 39 letters against a chance baseline of 36-39, where a synthetic two-digit cipher at the same transcription noise gives 207 - so the stream is not a two-digit substitution of that plaintext. outcome.notes: Contents in print since 1897 (Kiewning). The key was not recovered by this project: every attack here failed. It is the key of the sibling volume Barb.lat. 6956, broken by Biermann and Bosbach in 2018 and on DECODE R215; George Lasry had identified that it also serves 6960. Applied 21 Sept 2026, it reads all 28 ciphertexts except ~1,750 three-digit nomenclator groups absent from the key. The earlier finding of deterministic variable-length groups stands and is explained by the key (2-digit + 3-digit + 1-digit nulls). The catalogue said 'what the cipher hides is not known'; it is known, and has been in print since 1897, from the Roman office's own decipherments. The cipher itself was not broken here and no partial key is claimed: a held-out test shows the table learned from R286 predicts unseen text no better than a shuffled control (0.355 vs 0.359), so the 55% consistency of the first pass was overfitting. A positive control on synthetic ciphertext recovers a random key 100/100 from a clean transcription, 87/100 at 0.5% digit error and 7/100 at 1.7%, so the method is sound and the limit is the transcription. Two explanations remain open and cannot be separated from this material: length errors in the transcription, or the cipher not being a fixed-width substitution of this plaintext. The run-length control then settled that: the longest consistent two-digit run is 39 letters against a chance baseline of 36-39 (synthetic at the same noise: 207), so there is no alignment signal and noise is not a sufficient explanation. R286 is not a two-digit homophonic encipherment of Kiewning's Nr. 153. Open: whether the code width differs, whether the sheet encodes another despatch or a materially different wording, or whether the system is nomenclator-heavy or variable-length. A corpus search over all 1,161,303 letters of the edition then closed the first two: at widths 2, 3 and 4 no window of R286, R292, R306 or R311 enciphers any text printed in the volume, against a calibrated expectation of ~8 zero-false-positive hits on R286 alone. What survives is either a variable-length nomenclator, or text that is not in print because Kiewning gives it only as German regest.

A corpus search over all 1,161,303 letters of the edition then closed the first two: at widths 2, 3 and 4 no window of R286, R292, R306 or R311 enciphers any text printed in the volume, against a calibrated expectation of ~8 zero-false-positive hits on R286 alone. A corpus search over all 1,161,303 letters of the edition then closed the first two: at widths 2, 3 and 4 no window of R286, R292, R306 or R311 enciphers any text printed in the volume, against a calibrated expectation of ~8 zero-false-positive hits on R286 alone. title: Pallotto to Barberini, 1629 - 28 ciphered despatches of the nuncio at Vienna (BAV, Barb.lat. 6960)
system.summary: Two-digit homophonic substitution with syllable and common-word groups, three-digit nomenclator groups (200-999) for names and titles, and the digits 1 and 8 as nulls/word separators, written as a contiguous digit stream; the same key as Barb.lat. 6956 (1628), broken by Norbert Biermann and Thomas Bosbach in 2018.
system.sibling_key: Barb.lat. 6956 (1628), key recovered by Norbert Biermann and Thomas Bosbach, March 2018, filed on DECODE R215 (DOC_R215_D1506/D1507/D1508). George Lasry identified years ago that 6960 uses the same key; DECODE was never updated. Applied here 21 Sept 2026: it reads 6960.
system.notes: 112,805 digits over the 28 ciphertexts. Digit frequencies are uneven (0 = 16.1%, 4 = 4.8%) and adjacent digits carry ~0.18 bits of mutual information, so the stream is structured. A run-length control puts the longest consistent two-digit alignment to the known plaintext at 39 letters against a chance baseline of 36-39, where a synthetic two-digit cipher at the same transcription noise gives 207 - so the stream is not a two-digit substitution of that plaintext. CORRECTION 21 Sept 2026: the variable-length diagnosis was right, the rest of the system was not identified here. The key (sibling, 6956) mixes two-digit homophones, three-digit nomenclator groups and one-digit nulls 1/8, which is why every fixed-width test failed and why the repeat spectrum showed deterministic variable-length groups. distinct_symbols stays the digit alphabet; the key has ~127 known entries.

title: William Perwich to Lord Arlington, Paris, 9 April 1670, TNA SP 78/129 f. 180
system.summary: Columnar transposition with 20 columns, each written out as a line padded with nulls, framed by two null lines, with a few numeric nomenclator codes inside the plaintext.
system.sibling_key: none used
system.notes: Key as transcribed row numbers in plaintext column order: 15 20 19 17 18 21 16 14 2 4 3 5 6 7 13 12 11 10 9 8. Nulls: 47 column-tail cells plus the two null lines (23 + 9 cells). Nomenclator entries counted from the plaintext (40, 60, 61, 96, 97); 910 and 192 sit in the null tails.
conditions.prior_solution.where: TNA blog, 14 Oct 2025: broken independently by Matthew Brown and by Lasry, Biermann and Tomokiyo; plaintext in plaintext_tna.txt
conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.
conditions.tools: quadgram hill-climber over column order (solve20.py); chi-squared and digram-repeat tests (grid.py, routes.py); substitution solvers (masc.py, stream.py, segclimb.py)
outcome.method_basis: A complete decipherment already existed: the TNA published the plaintext on 14 Oct 2025 (Matthew Brown; Lasry, Biermann and Tomokiyo). The column order was reproduced here from Tomokiyo's transcription only after that announcement had given the system, and the project's own earlier substitution attack had failed.
outcome.contribution: none
outcome.notes: Solved by others in Oct 2025; this project first argued, wrongly, that it was a substitution, then reproduced the published break. The transposition key is complete; the nomenclator numbers are unread (40 probably a place, 60 96 and 61 persons). TNA context readings of the codes: 97 the Dutch, 60 and 61 the King, 96 Colbert, 40 England. No write-up: deciphered by others first (a page made 24 Sept 2026 was withdrawn the same day).
solution.kinds: transcription; statistics; solver; literature search; hypothesis; solver; verification; literature search; verification
doc.plaintext.source: Published decipherment announced by the National Archives on 14 Oct 2025 (Matthew Brown; independently George Lasry, Norbert Biermann and Satoshi Tomokiyo); TNA blog 'Secret diplomatic message deciphered after 350 years'. Copy in plaintext_tna.txt.
doc.transcription.source: Satoshi Tomokiyo's transcription (cryptiana blog, Sept 2025) of the TNA images published 4 Aug 2025
doc.transcription.notes: Measured with --skip '^[^\t]*$' (tab-separated cipher rows only). 494 cells include the clear word 'likelyhood' after the block; 493 cipher cells = 414 plaintext cells + 47 column-tail nulls + 32 cells in the two null lines (rows 1 and 22), which matches solve20.py report. title: Letter from Reims, 19 June [1589], on the Reims chapter's postulation, in the Nevers-Piles cipher, BnF fr. 20974 pp. 1-3 (DECODE R2276)
system.summary: Tomokiyo's Nevers-Piles symbol alphabet: homophones for the common letters, nulls, and code signs for short words, titles and names.

title: Four undeciphered intercepts in the Thurloe State Papers, 1653-56 (Birch 1742; cryptiana unsolved item #9)
system.summary: Four unrelated short ciphers: (a) figure substitution with a small code, (b) figures mixed with letters, (c) a ten-digit cipher, (d) homophonic figures with two codes.
system.sibling_key: Every 1653-60 royalist and Commonwealth key on cryptiana (Marshall, Barwick-Hyde, Stamford, Butler, Charles II intercepted, Kingston, Westrope, Hague agent/Blake) tried; none fits.
system.notes: Four separate systems, so types is undetermined for the set; NOTES read (a) as monoalphabetic letters plus a small code (8 code groups) and (d) as homophonic letters plus codes 226 243. nomenclator.entries counts the 10 code groups seen in (a) and (d).
conditions.prior_solution.where: Listed as undeciphered by Tomokiyo (cryptiana item #9); Birch's transcriptions are the only online witness and carry no decipherment.
conditions.human_role: unknown
conditions.tools: apply_keys.py (period keys scored by quadgram LM); solve_a2.py (simulated annealing, bijective and homophonic modes); stats_a.py (alphabetical-key search); lm_build.py (Dutch/French quadgram LMs); control.py (matched control for solve_a2.py)
outcome.method_basis: The four short intercepts printed in Birch's Thurloe State Papers resisted every 1653-60 key on cryptiana and quadgram annealing; a matched control shows piece (a) is long enough for the solver.
outcome.contribution: none
outcome.notes: Verdict STUCK: too short for cryptanalysis, no key online. Originals in Bodleian Rawlinson A, not digitised; sibling decipherments would be in the Nationaal Archief (a) and the Clarendon MSS (b-d), not online. Matched control run 2026-09-22 (control.py): the solver recovers synthetic texts of (a)'s layout (simple substitution 95-100%, 25-symbol homophonic 43-65% of trials), so the failure on (a) is meaningful, not a length artefact. The only commit (347fef4b5, 2026-09-15) has no model trailer.

system.summary: Mixed one-/two-digit monoalphabetic substitution (18 letters, u/v one code, no h, 9 = null, 81 = et) with unwritten code boundaries, plus a small layer of dotted pairs for ce/ci/qua/que/qui, non and three titles (Klee's key).
system.doubled_letters: written once (doubled digits strongly suppressed, 0.30 of chance; Farnese chancery rule 'senza duplicare le consonanti', Meister p. 223)
system.sibling_key: Spain IA-1 (DECODE R91, same volume, Dec 1541) is a different key; Meister 1906 keys nos. 1-3 (Montepulciano/Poggio 1539-42, Piacenza 1545) and Lasry's S6 key (1568-70) tested and excluded; none used.
system.notes: Null 9 occurs 365 times in Klee's alignment. The project's own diagnosis (4 = null, vowel digits {7,0,3,1}, Antonio Elio polyphonic-syllabic design) is superseded by Klee's key: 4 = o, 9 = null. distinct_symbols counts the 20 undotted codes plus 9 dotted codes of key.md.
